background_and_accessible_area_protocol.accessible_area_definition: Define an explicit accessible area (M) before background generation using host-range-informed ecoregion or biogeographic masks plus a documented dispersal buffer around vetted GBIF presences.

background_generation.design: Sample background points only inside the approved accessible-area mask and outside excluded nodata cells.
hard_blocks: no background sampling outside the approved accessible area
no use of human surveillance counts or human population surfaces as the target definition
background_generation.points_per_presence_guidance: target 5x to 20x as many background points as presences, capped by accessible-area size and raster resolution
sensitivity_sets: bias-aware background using a documented sampling-effort proxy or target-group background
buffer-width sensitivity using at least two alternative accessible-area extents

required_accessible_area_inputs: retained GBIF presence coordinates after QC and duplicate thinning review
host range or regional biogeographic support layer used to bound M
documented buffer distance or ecological justification for the accessible-area extent
land/sea mask and CRS-aligned model extent

requirements: Every extracted covariate layer must declare CRS, resolution, nodata, and resampling policy.
The manifest must identify the accessible area and background design used to create each extracted table.
Extraction outputs must preserve a join key back to each GBIF presence or generated background point.
Temporal mismatch between occurrence dates and static climatology must be disclosed in the manifest notes.

guardrails: This protocol defines a near-term formal gate only and does not fit a suitability model.
This artifact does not authorize or produce a formal risk map.
Any passed future gate must still be labeled host-occurrence suitability unless a separate human-risk target gate is approved.
WorldClim or other environmental covariates alone do not define risk.
Do not pool disparate host systems across continents without an explicit justification review.
Do not claim gate passage in this artifact.

pass_fail_qc_thresholds.fail_rule: Fail if any threshold is missed, if accessible area/background are undocumented, if folds are not spatially disjoint, or if target semantics drift toward human risk or abundance.
pass_fail_qc_thresholds.pass_rule: Near-term formal gate planning can be marked ready only if target semantics, accessible area, background design, covariate extraction manifest, and spatial block validation plan are all predeclared and all QC thresholds are met on the prepared modeling table.

recommended_target.presence_source: GBIF candidate host occurrence records that pass row-level QC and taxonomic screening
recommended_target.recommended_species_scope: single host species or tightly justified reservoir complex per regional model; avoid pooled cross-continental reservoir systems in the near-term formal gate
recommended_target.response_semantics: host occurrence suitability only; not human infection risk, not host abundance, and not spillover probability
recommended_target.response_unit: host occurrence record versus accessible-area background point

spatial_validation_protocol.design: Use spatially disjoint folds built from presence and background data within the accessible area, with fold construction documented before model fitting.

minimum_plan.holdout_rule: each validation fold must contain both presences and background rows after blocking
minimum_plan.leakage_guardrail: duplicate or near-duplicate coordinates cannot be split across train and validation folds

reporting_requirements: fold geometry description or block-generation rule
distance or block-size rationale tied to spatial autocorrelation risk
sensitivity note if alternative block sizes materially change discrimination
spatial_validation_protocol.strategy: Spatial block cross-validation only for the near-term formal gate.
